context: Checkpoint 2026-08-03 (late). The BUDGET LABORATORY shipped: 13 tasks, 33 commits, every task reviewed and three fix rounds spent. What exists now: a budget declared per dispatch on three axes (wall-clock deadline, cumulative tokens, estimated spend), resolved across three nested levels the way Kubernetes pairs ResourceQuota with LimitRange (node bounds what the machine can serve, workspace bounds within that, dispatch declares within both, and the record names WHICH level bound it); a durable BudgetObservation node per terminal effort carrying what governed the run, what it spent under OpenTelemetry's gen_ai.* names, and which rate table priced it; `refarm budget observations` to read it back; `refarm dispatch --budget-*` to declare it; and ceilings that actually bind. Proven end to end against the live daemon from the CLI: declared 120000, bound_by declared, max_tokens from the node default. The program began as a three-line symmetry fix and the operator refused to take it alone — 'a knob without a record manufactures the debt it was meant to remove'. That refusal is why the cost accounting underneath got audited, and the audit found SIX live defects nobody knew about, all predating this work: cache reads and writes summed despite being priced in opposite directions; Anthropic's uncached input priced at ZERO under any real cache rate; every Claude 5 model falling through to the return value that means 'local, free'; Groq, Together and Mistral defaults — paid APIs — classified as free; Haiku 4.5 carrying Haiku 3.5's retired rate; and Opus 4.5 and later inheriting Opus 4's price, over by THREE TIMES. No test would have caught any of them: the tests assert the formula uses the rate correctly, never that the rate matches the world.
current_tasks: SHIPPED — the budget laboratory, 13 tasks. packages/budget-contract-v1 (three axes, the three-level fold, 7 conformance checks mirrored byte-for-byte in Rust); the knob in dispatch; the sovereign config's top-level `budget` section (node + workspaces); BudgetObservation with flat gen_ai.* joins, max_usd.enforced, and rate_table_version; `refarm budget observations`; cumulative token and spend guards that bind; `--budget-*` on refarm dispatch and FARM_BUDGET_* in the phone kit. Scores at close: tractor 408 sidecar serial, agent 383, apps/refarm 2760, farm-client 213, all lanes green.

SHIPPED — the cost axis. rate_for_model answers Priced | Free-deleted | Unknown; every rate cites the vendor's official page (fetched and verified, which is HOW two wrong rates were found); RATE_TABLE_VERSION stamped on every observation so a later correction can find what to recompute; and check-model-defaults-drift now fails when a default model has no price, with a shrinking baseline of six known-unpriced defaults and a parse-sanity floor so a broken parse screams instead of passing clean.

OPEN — THE FIFTH GAP, found by the final review. NO effort builder anywhere sets `workspaceId`. Effort.workspace_id exists, workspace_budget_for early-returns on it, refarm.workspace.id is in the record, boundByWorkspace is in the summariser — and the value is always None. So D9's workspace level is STILL unreachable and `budget.workspaces` in the config can never bind. Task 9's commit message ('the workspace level of the budget fold becomes reachable') is not yet true. Fixing it needs a decision per surface about where the workspace identity comes from.

OPEN — refarm.outcome.steps_completed / .steps_planned are hardcoded None at the only production caller (observation.rs). F1 named TWO things missing from the record: the ceiling that applied, and the step the run reached. This program recorded the first. 'Died at 4/25', the measurement that originated the whole design, is still not recoverable. The agent knows its steps; the sidecar does not; closing it means the agent reporting them.

OPEN — packages/health's ConfigNodeAuditor has NEVER audited a real replicated node. sidecar-client's graph client requires every node to carry `@context` and the Rust sidecar never sets it (grep '@context' packages/tractor/src returns nothing), so the auditor's try/catch turns the throw into a soft 'audit skipped' note. Its entire purpose is cross-device config-drift detection. `refarm health` — the command CLAUDE.md tells every agent to run — contains a check that has always passed by never running. resolveSovereignConfig degrades the same way. Entirely pre-existing; deserves its own spec.

OPEN — the previous phase's items, unchanged: prompt-contract-v1 file size and the farm-client single-file vendor constraint; observer::tests::rotate_seals flaky under parallel cargo test --lib; `refarm resume` reporting the daily-handoff automation as scheduled when nothing executes it; CI quality exit 101 in tractor needing fresh evidence.
next_actions: The credential scope, verb to verb×object (`start-operations` becomes `start-operations@<workspace>`), decided with the maintainer on 2026-08-03 to come BEFORE spec slices 6-8. The arithmetic is why: Scope is a closed enum of three variants and scoped-credential.v1 has almost nothing issued against it, so widening now is a toy migration and widening later is a v2 plus a coexistence window. It inherits two prerequisites this program built: the effort carrying its workspace identity, and resolve_axis written as nested POLICY resolution with budget as its first consumer rather than its definition. Note it also needs the fifth gap closed — nothing sets workspaceId yet.

GitHub Copilot as a real provider, and the fourth budget axis it will demand. It is already half-present: SUBSCRIPTION_MODEL_PROVIDERS lists it, it has an env key and a default model, and the new price gate correctly exempts it — but RUNTIME_SUBSCRIPTION_MODEL_PROVIDERS holds only openai-codex and provider_config gives it no base URL. Missing: a Rust route and a GitHub OAuth device flow. When it lands it will NOT fit any of the three axes: its binding constraint is requests per billing period, a quota that refills, and the whole point of running work there is to spend quota that would otherwise idle. BudgetDeclaration's fields are all optional, so the fourth axis is additive when the pressure is real.

Then spec slices 6-8 (the sweep, the gallery, closing the loop). By then the record holds real observations, which is what slice 8 needs to derive a default and a ceiling from evidence instead of from a constant. Prerequisite noted by the final review: refarm.elapsed_ms is second-quantised, so any run under one second records 0 — load-bearing for slice 6's completion-rate-under-budget metric.
open_questions: Where does the workspace identity come from, per surface? `refarm dispatch` has no workspace context; a declared operation (workspace:rcdc5:code-boundaries) does. Answering this closes the fifth gap and unblocks both the workspace ceiling and the verb×object credential scope.

Should the observation record which axes were ENFORCED, not just which were declared? The fix wave added max_usd.enforced because a currency ceiling cannot bind outside api pricing mode. The same question applies to the other two: on the event-dispatch path no axis binds at all (now correctly omitted), and within the respond path three sub-cases — a task-less effort, an agent-not-loaded channel miss, a channel-send error — still record a full budget family with no watcher having run. Parked as milder than the defect it came from; a per-axis `enforced` would settle the class rather than the instances.

How does the CLI learn the CURRENT rate table? It now derives it from the newest observation's own stamp, which detects relative staleness among observed runs but cannot see the cold-start case: bump RATE_TABLE_VERSION, run nothing, and every record is stale while stalePricing reports zero. The real fix publishes the constant out of the WASM guest.
